# cpuload

Monitor CPU load by reading /proc/stat in a loop.

Outputs time-series results `TLOAD-<timestamp>-RESULT-CPU-<id>` with the per-core
utilization percentage. Use the variables `CPUMIN`/`CPUMAX` to select a range of cores,
`CPUTHRESH` to only start reporting after utilization exceeds a threshold,
and `CPUSUM=1` to aggregate all cores into a single `CPUSUM` result.

Usage:
```bash
%import@server cpuload CPUMIN=0 CPUMAX=16
```

Source: [`modules/cpuload.npf`](https://github.com/tbarbette/npf/blob/main/modules/cpuload.npf)

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CPUMIN` | `0` | First core to monitor |
| `CPUMAX` | `128` | Monitor cores up to this one, excluded |
| `CPUTHRESH` | `1` | Only start reporting once a core exceeds this utilization percentage, 0 to report from the start |
| `CPUSUM` | `0` | Report the sum of the utilization of all monitored cores instead of one result per core |
